reader.requirement: At --std 85, FUNCTION INTEGER-PART of a negative class-numeric argument (any usage, scale, P-scaling, literal or arithmetic expression, up to 18 digits) returns the least integer >= the argument, i.e. truncation toward zero (-1.5 -> -1, -0.5 -> 0); the function may appear only in an arithmetic expression.

edition-consulted.switches: D8 edition window: sig.IntroducedIn (85 for the 1989 module rows, IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build) against ctx.Edition.DialectLevel; COBOL1502/1503 outside it

ConstructRegistry NumericFunctionIdentifierOperand2002: at 85 a numeric/integer function written where an identifier stands (MOVE sender) is refused (COBOL0900), per §1989:A.2.3 GR2/GR3; never reached inside an arithmetic expression
Edition.DigitCapacityExcess: 18-digit cap on items and literals at 85 (31 later); bounds the argument range only
num.StandardDecimal (OPTIONS ARITHMETIC, a 2002+ paragraph, so always native at 85): the native dispatch is the one a 2023 program with no ARITHMETIC clause takes

reader.edition-search: grep of IntrinsicBinder.cs, IntrinsicRenderer.cs, IntrinsicCarrierRules.cs, FunctionValueLane.cs for Edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion|ArithmeticMode|StandardDecimal; the runtime bodies take no edition input
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the returned value is the same native Truncate arm (Int128 / 10^scale, toward zero) at 85 and 2023; only the 18-digit argument cap and the identifier-operand refusal differ
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers -1.5, -1.0, -0.5, -0.25 on one S9V99 DISPLAY item; not the 18-digit extreme, COMP/COMP-3, P-scaling, literal and expression arguments, ODO element, or a subscript the statement changes

probes.printed: COBOL1627 for alphanumeric, numeric-edited, group, nonnumeric literal and ref-modified arguments; COBOL1504 for two arguments
probes.expected: refused: argument-1 must be class numeric (§1989:A.2.18.3 AR1), one argument

probes.printed: first build (ip1-002): MOVE FUNCTION INTEGER-PART(A-M15) TO SDX refused COBOL0900 (requires COBOL-2002)
probes.expected: refused at 85: an integer function may be used only in an arithmetic expression (§1989:A.2.3 GR3)

probes.printed: COBOL0802 for PIC S9(19); COBOL0900 for USAGE FLOAT-LONG
probes.expected: refused at 85: 18-digit maximum, no floating usage

citations.check: OK  §1989:A.2.18.4 RV3  (2.18.4 Returned Values)  the text is in RV3
OK  §1989:A.2.3 GR3  (2.3 TYPES OF FUNCTIONS)  the text is in GR3

reader.notes: The native Truncate body divides the scaled Int128 by 10^scale, which truncates toward zero, so every negative argument gets the least integer >= it. Every probe output was identical at --std 2023 (at2023-ip1.txt). The refusal diagnostics cite the 2023 clause numbers, not §1989, which is cosmetic for this rule.

refuter.evidence: rip1-003 (--std 85): S9(17)V9 -99999999999999999.9 -> -99999999999999999; SV9(18) DISPLAY and COMP-3 -.999999999999999999 -> 0; S9(18) COMP -999999999999999999 unchanged; SPPP9 -.0009 -> 0; S9(3)PPP -123000 -> -123000; SIGN LEADING SEPARATE -7.25 and SIGN TRAILING -7.75 -> -7; -10/4 -> -2; X/Y (-0.6667) -> 0; X**3 (-8.0012) -> -8; INTEGER-PART(SIN(-2)) -> 0; SQRT(2)*-1 -> -1; LOG(10)*-100 -> -230; relation condition = -2 true; IS ZERO true and IS NEGATIVE false for INTEGER-PART(-.999...), IS POSITIVE false for INTEGER-PART(-0.5). -1/3*3 -> 0 is the intermediate-result technique the implementor indicates (§1985:VI.6.2.3 GR6), not this rule. rref1-001: floating literal -1.5E0 argument refused COBOL0900 at 85. rplace1-001: ADD FUNCTION INTEGER-PART(X) TO R refused COBOL0900 (not an arithmetic expression, §1989:A.2.3 GR2/GR3). cite.py: 'OK  §1989:A.2.18.4 RV3  (2.18.4 Returned Values)  the text is in RV3'; 'OK  §1985:VI.6.2.3 ... it lies in GR6'.
